html:
Cayenne is the capital of French Guiana, on an island at the mouth of the Cayenne River. French settlers tried to settle there from the 1640s, and from 1664 they held it for good, apart from brief Dutch, English and Portuguese occupations.

The colony grew slowly. A few plantations of sugar, coffee, cacao and annatto were worked by enslaved Africans. Disease and the dense forest kept the settler population small, and the land was used more for exile than for profit.

Cayenne stayed a small port while the penal colony and later the space centre gave French Guiana its fame. It became the capital of an overseas department of France in 1946.
